aiMemory.previousSummary:
73-year-old male with HFrEF (EF 30-35%, Dx prior to 2022), CKD Stage 3b (baseline Cr ~2.0, eGFR 34-42 trending downward), T2DM on insulin with diabetic neuropathy (A1c improving: 8.5% → 7.8% → 7.3% → 7.2%), persistent AFib (off anticoagulation since GI hemorrhage 9/2023), HTN, hyperlipidemia, obesity (BMI 33), and BPH. On quadruple GDMT including Entresto, carvedilol, spironolactone, and furosemide; empagliflozin added May 2025. NYHA Class II at baseline (2 blocks flat, 1 flight stairs with pausing). Active medication count now confirmed at 15.

Recent hospitalization 9/6-9/10/2025 for ADHF (NYHA III-IV on admission, BNP 1,240, AKI Cr 2.3, mild hyperkalemia K 5.1) precipitated by dietary sodium excess over Labor Day weekend. Successfully diuresed to baseline weight ~97 kg at discharge 9/10/2025. Sustained mechanical fall 9/12/2025 (2:30 AM bathroom trip) — ED eval negative for fracture/intracranial pathology. Current vitals show weight 99.5 kg, which is +2-2.5 kg above the recently established dry weight of 97-97.5 kg, meeting the patient's action threshold for diuretic adjustment. SpO2 96% on RA is mildly reduced and warrants evaluation for early re-decompensation. HR now 70 (improved rate control vs. 84 on prior admission). BP 133/86 is within prior range.

Fall risk remains multifactorial and inadequately mitigated: diabetic peripheral neuropathy, nocturia 2-3x nightly (BPH + furosemide + empagliflozin), and environmental hazards. ICD candidacy has been deferred since 2022; patient and wife increasingly open to discussion. Anticoagulation remains withheld post-GI bleed — ongoing risk-benefit tension given persistent AFib.
problemInsights: Weight trend since 9/2025 discharge shows recurrent oscillation (97-102.7kg) with at least one transient decompensation episode (~1/28/26) that self-resolved; suggests fragile volume status requiring close outpatient monitoring and possible diuretic regimen reinforcement rather than single dry-weight target being reliably maintained.
